X.label: X axis, a diameter
X.description: Position across the turning axis, written as a diameter while diameter programming is on. With G4 it is a dwell time in seconds.

U.label: Incremental X, a diameter
U.description: Distance to move across the turning axis, as a diameter. Inside the multi-pass cycles it is a depth of cut or an allowance on X instead, and with G4 a dwell time in seconds.

W.label: Incremental Z
W.description: Distance to move along the turning axis. Inside the multi-pass cycles it is a depth of cut or an allowance on Z instead.

C.label: C axis
C.description: Angle of the spindle, used to place holes and flats for driven tools.

R.label: Radius, retract or allowance
R.description: Arc radius with G2 and G3. In the lathe cycles it is the retract between passes, a taper, a relief amount or a finish allowance, depending on the cycle and on the block.

F.label: Feed, or thread lead
F.description: Feed rate. The unit follows the feed mode: distance per minute with G98, per spindle revolution with G99. In a threading block it is the thread lead instead.

E.label: Thread lead, fine form
E.description: A thread lead written more precisely than F allows, on controls that offer it. Not confirmed against the syntax notes; check what your control does with it.

P.label: Block reference, dwell, step or program number
P.description: First profile block with G70 to G73, a dwell in least time increments with G4 (1 ms on IS-B), a step in least increments with G74 and G75, the packed thread data of G76, or the program number with M98.

Q.label: Block reference, peck or cut depth
Q.description: Last profile block with G70 to G73, a peck in microns with G74, G75, G83 and G87, the first cut depth of G76, or the block a local call starts at with M98.

T.label: Turret station and offset
T.description: The last two digits are the offset register and the ones before them the turret station, so T0101 and T101 are both station 1 with offset 1. An offset of 00 cancels the offset and is not a tool change.

H.label: H address
H.description: Not described for turning in the syntax notes. Some controls read it as an incremental C move. Check what your control does with it.

D.label: D address
D.description: Usually not used for turning: the nose radius and the tip direction come from the tool offset the T word selects. Magazine-type machines may use it as an offset register.

codes.label: Dwell
codes.description: Holds the tool where it is before the next block runs. It applies to this block only.

params.label: Dwell time in seconds
Dwell time in seconds
Dwell time (least time increments: 1 ms on IS-B)

codes.label: ZX plane, the turning plane
codes.description: Selects ZX as the working plane, which is where turning happens. Arcs use I and K. Lathes come up in this plane and CAM output rarely leaves it.

codes.label: Thread cutting pass
codes.description: Cuts one straight or tapered threading pass to the end point in the block. F is the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate, so scaling the feed would change the thread. G-code system B spells this G33.

params.label: Thread end diameter
Thread end along Z
Thread lead per revolution

codes.label: Cancel nose radius compensation
codes.description: Turns nose radius compensation off. Do it during a retract move, not in an arc.

codes.label: Nose radius compensation, tool left
codes.description: Offsets the path by the insert nose radius to the left of the direction of travel. The radius and the tip direction come from the tool offset the T word selects, so no register is written in the block. Switch it on during an approach move.

codes.label: Nose radius compensation, tool right
codes.description: Offsets the path by the insert nose radius to the right of the direction of travel. The radius and the tip direction come from the tool offset the T word selects, so no register is written in the block. Switch it on during an approach move.

codes.label: Coordinate set, top spindle speed
codes.description: Sets the coordinate system without moving. With an S word it gives the highest spindle speed the control may use for constant surface speed; write it in a block of its own in front of G96. G-code system B uses G92 for this.

codes.label: Work coordinate system preset
codes.description: Puts the work coordinate system back where its work offset says, after a manual move or a shift has displaced it. The block names the axes to reset, each with 0; an axis it does not name keeps its coordinates. This is the G-code system A spelling; systems B and C write G92.1.

codes.label: Mirror image for the second turret
codes.description: On a lathe with two opposed turrets, mirrors the moves so that the second turret machines the same shape (mirror image, or symmetric machining). G69 ends it. A machining centre uses the same number for a rotation of the coordinate system.

codes.label: Coordinate system rotation
codes.description: Turns the coordinates of the following blocks about a centre in the selected plane by the angle R, positive counter-clockwise (absolute, unless a machine parameter makes it incremental). The two axis words of the plane give the centre, always absolute; without them the tool position is the centre, and without R a machine parameter gives the angle. With X, Y, Z and I, J, K the same code starts a three-dimensional coordinate conversion about the direction I, J, K. G69.1 ends both. The first move after G68.1 and after G69.1 has to be absolute.

params.label: Rotation angle, positive counter-clockwise
Rotation axis direction, X component (three-dimensional conversion)
Rotation axis direction, Y component (three-dimensional conversion)
Rotation axis direction, Z component (three-dimensional conversion)

codes.label: Tilted working plane
codes.description: Defines a coordinate system tilted against the workpiece and makes it the one the program is written in. X, Y and Z give its origin; I, J and K give the three Euler angles, or with P another way to define the plane (P1 roll-pitch-yaw angles with Q as the order of the turns, P2 three points, P3 two vectors, P4 projection angles). On the lathe G69.1 ends it (G69 ends the mirror image of the second turret). G53.1 in the next block turns the rotary axes to the new tool direction.

params.label: How the plane is defined: none Euler angles, 1 to 4 another form

codes.label: Tilted working plane from the tool direction
codes.description: Makes the coordinate system whose Z axis is the present direction of the tool the one the program is written in. X, Y and Z give its origin in absolute values (the present position when left out); R turns it about its Z axis. On the lathe G69.1 ends it (G69 ends the mirror image of the second turret).

params.label: Turn about the new Z axis

codes.label: Tilted working plane, added to the one in force
codes.description: Tilts again, relative to the tilted plane that is in force. It is written like G68.2 (P chooses the form), and its origin is given in the coordinates of that plane. Tool length and radius compensation must be off. On the lathe G69.1 ends it (G69 ends the mirror image of the second turret).

params.label: How the plane is defined: none Euler angles, 1 to 4 another form

codes.label: Mirror image for the second turret off
codes.description: Ends the mirror image that G68 started. A machining centre uses the same number to end a rotation of the coordinate system.

codes.label: Coordinate system rotation off
codes.description: Ends G68.1 (the rotation or the three-dimensional conversion) and the tilted working plane of G68.2, and goes back to the coordinates of the program. It may stand in a block with other words; the first move after it has to be absolute.

codes.label: Finishing pass along the profile
codes.description: Runs the finishing pass along the profile blocks from P to Q, taking the feed and speed written inside those blocks. It follows a roughing cycle that left an allowance.

codes.label: Roughing cycle along Z
codes.description: Roughs an outside or inside contour in passes along Z and leaves a finishing allowance for G70. Written in two blocks: the depth of cut and the retract first, then the profile range, the allowances and the feed. The block with P and Q runs the cycle; the same U means the depth of cut in the first block and the allowance on X in the second. The first block's values are machine parameters that the block overwrites, so they stay in force until written again. The addresses are those of the usual ZX plane (G18); in another plane the control reads other ones.

codes.label: Roughing cycle along X (facing)
codes.description: The same as G71, but the passes run along X, so it roughs a face instead of a diameter. Written in two blocks: the depth of cut (W) and the retract first, then the profile range, the allowances and the feed. The block with P and Q runs the cycle; the same W means the depth of cut in the first block and the allowance on Z in the second. The first block's values are machine parameters that the block overwrites, so they stay in force until written again. The addresses are those of the usual ZX plane (G18); in another plane the control reads other ones.

codes.label: Pattern repeating cycle
codes.description: Walks the profile again and again, each time a little closer to the finished shape. It suits a blank that is already near the final form, such as a casting or a forging. Written in two blocks: the relief on X and Z and the number of passes first, then the profile range, the allowances and the feed. The block with P and Q runs the cycle. The first block's values are machine parameters that the block overwrites, so they stay in force until written again. The addresses are those of the usual ZX plane (G18); in another plane the control reads other ones.

codes.label: Face pecking cycle
codes.description: Drills or grooves into the face in pecks along Z, backing off between them so the chips break. Written in two blocks: the back-off amount first, then the end point, the steps, the relief at the bottom and the feed. The block with an axis word runs the cycle; R means the back-off in the first block and the relief at the bottom in the second. Without X (U) and P it only pecks along Z: a deep-hole drilling cycle. On a lathe it is not a tapping cycle, so F is an ordinary feed, but the same number is the left-hand tapping cycle on a mill, where F is the pitch. gEdit scales neither the F of such a block nor the spindle speed it runs at: refusing a real pecking feed costs one edit by hand, scaling a pitch or the speed of a tap cuts a different thread.

codes.label: Grooving cycle along X
codes.description: The same as G74 turned through ninety degrees: it pecks into a diameter along X and steps along Z, which is how a wide groove is cut with a narrow insert. Written in two blocks: the back-off amount first, then the end point, the steps, the relief at the bottom and the feed. The block with an axis word runs the cycle; R means the back-off in the first block and the relief at the bottom in the second. Without Z (W) and Q it cuts one groove, or parts off.

codes.label: Multi-pass threading cycle
codes.description: Cuts a thread in several passes, taking less material each time. Written in two blocks: the finishing passes, the pull-out chamfer and the insert angle packed into P, the smallest depth of cut and the finishing allowance first; then the end point, the taper, the thread height, the depth of the first cut and the lead. The block with X (U) and Z (W) runs the cycle; P, Q and R mean different things in the two blocks, and each of them stays in force until it is written again. F is the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate. gEdit shows both P values as written: the packed digits of the first block must never be converted.

params.label: Six digits packed: number of finishing passes (01-99), pull-out chamfer in tenths of the lead (00-99), insert angle (80, 60, 55, 30, 29 or 00 degrees); P010060 is one pass, no chamfer, 60°. Counted, never converted

codes.label: Turning pass (G-code system B)
codes.description: G-code system A does not use this number; in system B it is the single-pass turning cycle that system A writes as G90. Its F is an ordinary feed. A program that writes it was almost certainly posted for system B, so set a machine with that G-code system to read it properly.

codes.label: Threading pass (G-code system B)
codes.description: G-code system A does not use this number; in system B it is the single-pass threading cycle that system A writes as G92, and its F is the thread lead per revolution. gEdit therefore never scales the F of such a block, whichever G-code system the document is read in: a program that writes G78 was almost certainly posted for system B. Set a machine with that G-code system to read the rest of the program properly.

codes.label: Facing pass (G-code system B)
codes.description: G-code system A does not use this number; in system B it is the single-pass facing cycle that system A writes as G94. Its F is an ordinary feed. A program that writes it was almost certainly posted for system B, so set a machine with that G-code system to read it properly.

codes.label: Cancel the drilling cycle
codes.description: Ends the active drilling, tapping or boring cycle. Any code from the motion group ends it as well.

codes.label: Drilling cycle on the face
codes.description: Drills along Z into the face of the part, on centre or on a C position under a driven tool. With Q it pecks. It stays active, so the next block with a position drills another hole, until G80.

codes.label: Turning pass
codes.description: Cuts one outside or inside turning pass, straight or tapered, and returns to the start point. It belongs to the motion group, so the next G00 or G01 ends it. On a mill and in G-code system B the same number means absolute positions instead.

params.label: End diameter of the pass

codes.label: Threading pass as a cycle
codes.description: Cuts one threading pass, straight or tapered, and returns to the start point, so a thread is written as a list of X values. F is the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate. On a mill and in G-code system B the same number sets the coordinate system and clamps the spindle speed instead. A threading pass carries no S word, so gEdit reads the S of a G92 block as that speed clamp rather than as a speed to scale — which is what protects a system-B program opened with a system-A machine.

codes.label: Facing pass
codes.description: Cuts one facing pass, square or tapered, and returns to the start point. It belongs to the motion group, so the next G00 or G01 ends it. On a mill and in G-code system B the same number means feed per minute instead; on a lathe in system A the feed modes are G98 and G99.

codes.label: Constant surface speed
codes.description: S is read as a surface speed in metres per minute, or feet per minute in the inch system, and the control raises the spindle speed as the diameter gets smaller. Clamp the top speed with G50 in a block of its own beforehand.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed
codes.description: S is read as revolutions per minute again and the speed stays where it is set. Threading and drilling on centre need it.

codes.label: Feed per minute
codes.description: F is read as distance per minute. This is what G98 means in G-code system A; on a mill and in system B the same number chooses the level a drilling cycle returns to.

codes.label: Feed per revolution
codes.description: F is read as distance per spindle revolution, which keeps the chip thickness steady while constant surface speed changes the spindle speed. This is what G99 means in G-code system A; on a mill and in system B the same number chooses the level a drilling cycle returns to.

codes.label: Tool change on a magazine machine
codes.description: Changes to the tool that T selects on a machine with a tool magazine. A turret indexes on the T word alone and does not use M6.
